gen-dafont-joystix-gf-saira: Joystix spaces its bold arcade letters wide and keeps the stems barely heavier than the arms joining them. And Saira follows in a plain sans with rounded, tall letters and an s you can see straight through.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sarpanch: Approachable is the first thing Sarpanch gives off, with a clearly open e and a compact build under Joystix's loud arcade heading. And a long stretch of it would read smoothly, since the sans-serif letters stay compact and never crowd each other.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Joystix brings a bold arcade look, widely tracked and gently weighted. Schibsted Grotesk below it is a sans-serif with tall-bowled a and e shapes and terminals that never close in, so paragraphs of it feel welcoming and unhurried.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sen: Joystix is bold and arcade, its bowls swelling only slightly. Sen, a plain sans built tall with one constant line like a drawn cable, keeps a long passage modern and steady, its curves ending before they turn inward.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sintony: Sintony is clean and contemporary, with a chunky, tall midzone. A longer passage in this plain sans reads smoothly because no curve clogs, while Joystix adds its widely tracked arcade heading above with thin strokes of respectable weight.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sofia-sans: Sofia Sans reads modern and tidy, a sans-serif with no thick-and-thin modulation and tall lowercase like cut acrylic stencil pieces. Joystix does the loud arcade swagger, with a faint crayon-like rhythm; Sofia Sans does the quiet carrying.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-sofia-sans-semi-co: Lowercase that nearly matches the capitals in height gives this body a clean, stencil-cut feel, with a big visible entrance into each curve. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed, a plain sans of wire-like constant strokes, sits under Joystix's bold arcade heading as its steadier counterpart.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-stack-sans-headlin: Stack Sans Headline reads professional and approachable, with a deep middle band and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. And Joystix, bold and arcade, makes the strongest single quality of the pair its gap in stroke character against that sans-serif's single constant width.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-stack-sans-notch: Joystix lays out bold arcade letters with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. Stack Sans Notch, a sans-serif of rod-stock strokes and big-bodied lowercase, can be sized down comfortably without losing its open curves.
gen-dafont-joystix-gf-stack-sans-text: Wide tracking is the loudest trait of Joystix, an arcade heading with a faint upstroke-downstroke weight difference. Stack Sans Text, a sans-serif drawn like a marker with well-spaced curve endings, makes the pair's strongest quality its unshaded body texture against that playful heading.
